tool_plan.objective: Generate and preserve representative Chromium web-cache content that ChromeCacheView can parse and display with cache metadata.

required_actions.name: browser.launch
required_actions.why: Starts the Chromium session that creates the target Chrome cache.

required_actions.name: browser.goto
required_actions.why: Loads distinct documents and network resources into the browser cache.

required_actions.name: browser.get_clickables
required_actions.why: Observes visible controls and finite choices before exercising cache-relevant page states.

required_actions.name: browser.click
required_actions.why: Commits observed links or controls that load additional cacheable resources.

required_actions.name: browser.smart_type
required_actions.why: Performs realistic query or form input that can produce distinct cached responses.

required_actions.name: browser.select_option
required_actions.why: Changes observed finite page parameters that can request materially different resources.

required_actions.name: browser.scroll
required_actions.why: Reveals lazy-loaded or progressive content that may add cached assets.

required_actions.name: browser.screenshot
required_actions.why: Preserves a representation of visible content associated with generated cache activity.

required_actions.name: browser.close
required_actions.why: Closes the browser to help flush cache writes before collection.

completion.detail: Complete after Chromium has been closed and the generated Chromium cache data is present for collection and parsing by ChromeCacheView.

tool_plan.action_intent_guidance: Action Flow: Launch Chromium and use run-provided runtime resources with browser.goto to visit pages likely to load ordinary cacheable documents, images, scripts, styles, and media. On each relevant page, use browser.get_clickables to inspect visible controls; use browser.click only on observed navigation or content controls that load additional visible resources. Where visible search or form input is available, use browser.smart_type to request a distinct response, and use browser.select_option for observed finite choices that change displayed content or requested resources. Use browser.scroll to reveal progressive or lazy-loaded content, then re-run browser.get_clickables after the reveal and perform a bounded observe -> reveal -> re-observe cycle when new visible controls or content appear. Capture browser.screenshot while representative loaded content is visible. Visit a few distinct runtime-provided pages or page states, then close Chromium with browser.close so cache writes are flushed. This activity should produce chromium.cache.cache_data containing cache entries and associated metadata. Reason guidance: write context-specific reasons that state the page activity and expect
